tasks.title: Catch the renewal that skips a month
tasks.description:
Prove the bug with a test before you change `renewals.js`. In `src/renewals.test.js`, write tests in the `describe('the ticket')` block that fail on the shop's `renewsOn()` today, on any computer, and will pass once it is right.

The check runs the tests in that block on three computers beside:

- the shop's `renewals.js`: they must fail on every one
- a right fix: they must pass
- a version that mends only the ticket's own renewal: they must fail
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.js` and look at Ängsö's first renewal.
Write the date a licence that starts on 31 January should renew on.
Add another start on a day that the next month does not have.
Run `npx vitest run src/renewals.test.js` and see your tests fail.
hints: The ticket's licence started on the 31st, and February has no 31st.
The shop's rule keeps the day, or takes the last day of a month that is too short for it. 31 March plus one month is the same kind of case.
expect(renewsOn('2026-01-31', 1)).toBe(...) with the last day of February 2026, and one more start such as 31 March or 31 August.

tasks.title: Add months and days the way a calendar does
tasks.description:
Fix both functions in `src/renewals.js` so they follow the calendar on any computer.

`renewsOn(started, months)` returns the calendar date, as text like `'2026-02-28'`, that a licence renews on after that many months:

- it keeps the start's day of the month
- when that month is too short, it is the month's last day: 28 February, or 29 in a leap year
- months always count from the start date, so two months after 31 January is 31 March

`remindAt(sendAt, days)` returns the same time of day that many calendar days later, written the same way, like `'2026-04-01T09:00'`. The time is shop time, written without a zone.

The check uses its own dates, month ends, leap years and the nights the clocks change, on five computers.
nextSteps: Read the start date as its year, month and day numbers.
Work out the last day of the month the renewal lands in, and keep the day inside it.
For a follow-up, add days to the date and keep the time of day as it was written.
Run `node src/demo.js`: both blocks should agree.
hints: `setUTCMonth` on the 31st rolls into the next month when the target month is shorter, and `getTime() + days * DAY_MS` assumes every day on the computer's clock is 24 hours.
`Date.UTC(year, month, 0)` is the last day of the month before `month`, counted from 0, and in UTC every day is 24 hours long. `Date.UTC` also rolls day 32 or month 13 over for you.

For `renewsOn`, take `Math.min(day, lastDay)` in the target month and build it with `Date.UTC`. For `remindAt`, split off the time, build `Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day + days)`, and put the time back on the date.

tasks.title: Write the tests for the cases next door
tasks.description:
Two cases sit next to the ticket: a renewal that lands at the end of February in a leap year, and a follow-up across the night the clocks change. In the `describe('next door')` block, write a test for each.

The check runs the tests in that block on three computers beside the shop's `renewals.js` (they must fail on every one), beside a right fix (they must pass), beside a version that gives February 28 days every year (they must fail) and beside a version that adds a follow-up's days as blocks of 24 hours (they must fail).
nextSteps: Pick a start date whose renewal lands in February 2028.
Pick a follow-up whose week has the night London's clocks change.
hints: 2028 is a leap year. The clocks in London go forward on the last Sunday of March and back on the last Sunday of October.
A follow-up only goes wrong on a computer whose clock changes that night, so the test has to say which zone it runs in.
expect(renewsOn('2028-01-31', 1)).toBe(...) for the leap year, and inZone('Europe/London', () => expect(remindAt('2026-03-25T09:00', 7)).toBe(...)) for the clock change.
